title: Product workshop
subtitle: From customer evidence to an engineering handoff
intro: The practical value is a repeatable workflow: give specialists authoritative context, preserve their standards, and make each handoff explicit. Human review remains part of the delivery process.
actions: Product researcher: customer evidence and requirements. Designer: approved design system and examples. Engineering coordinator: technical decomposition and review. Add an analyst when you have reliable data sources.
PE application: use your existing standards and skills as the shared foundation. This is a suggested starting arrangement, not the exact team shown.
Provide your requirements template, previous good specifications, customer evidence, design assets, coding standards, and source-of-truth links. Define which document wins if sources disagree.
Done when a specialist can produce the right format without another explanation.
Require each handoff to include the current document, scope, acceptance criteria, unresolved decisions, and the next responsible role. Put collaborating roles in a project conversation.
Done when research can become a reviewed specification without manually copying context.
Ask for citations and dates. For analytics, specify canonical tables, metric definitions, time windows, and known querying pitfalls.
The workshop emphasizes that curated data is a prerequisite for trusted analysis.
Have a coordinator summarize where communication and document activity indicate your attention went. Compare that with your stated priorities.
PE application: identify customer interruptions or operational work displacing planned delivery.
Monitor a small set of outcomes
Choose product or operational metrics you can act on. Set a regular summary and ask for investigation when a meaningful change appears.
Start at a useful frequency; the workshop demonstrates hourly monitoring, not a universal requirement.
prompts: Your role is product research and requirements preparation. Use the linked PE standards, requirements template, and customer evidence. Cite sources, distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions, and identify missing decisions. Prepare drafts for review.

Prepare a requirements draft using our template and the linked customer evidence. Define the problem, affected users, proposed first version, out-of-scope work, acceptance criteria, and unresolved questions. Link the supporting evidence and hand the draft over for review before implementation.

Review this approved requirements document and design. Identify dependencies, technical tasks, and verification needed. Preserve the scope and acceptance criteria. Surface blockers and decisions requiring my input before starting dependent work.

Compare my stated priorities with the activity in the sources provided for this week. Summarize where my attention went, identify divergences, and link the evidence. Suggest the three most useful changes for next week.
